title: Studying in Italy from zero
subtitle: From your first question to your first day in Italy: a complete guide
letter:
Hello!

If you have opened this page, there is probably one question on your mind: «Can I study in Italy too?». The answer is often «yes». But the road is long, the terms are unfamiliar (pre-acceptance, DoV, Universitaly, permesso...) and the internet is full of contradictory advice. That is why many people do not know where to start and miss the most important deadlines.

This guide was written exactly for that reason. It explains everything in order and in plain language for someone who knows nothing yet: what to do, when to do it, which document you need and where people most often go wrong.

Take your time. Read each chapter, mark what you need, and do only one step at a time. The road looks long, but each step on its own is simple.

summary.d: Level, field, 3–5 universities, language and tests.
University application; if they say «we will take you», a pre-acceptance letter arrives.
Diploma recognition: DoV from the embassy or an online CIMEA certificate.
Application on the Universitaly portal; the university confirms it.
Type D student visa at the Italian Embassy in Tashkent.
Family documents are prepared in Uzbekistan, the application is submitted in summer.
SIM card, transport card, permesso, codice fiscale and bank: in the right order.
You hand in your original documents and become a full student.

chapters.title: First, ask yourself 5 questions
chapters.when: 2–3 months before applications open (usually summer – autumn)
chapters.body:
The decision to go to Italy starts not with collecting documents but with a clear goal. Everything that follows (which test, which document, which deadline, how much money) depends on that goal.

Write honest answers to the questions below on paper. If you do not know an answer, do not worry: the rest of this chapter is exactly about that.
steps: Which level am I applying for? Foundation, bachelor's (3 years) or master's (2 years).
Which field? Economics, engineering, IT, medicine, international relations...
In which language will I study? There are many English-taught programmes: if you study in English, Italian is not required.
Which city? A big city is exciting, but housing is expensive. A small university town is cheaper and quieter.
Who shows the money? The visa requires {{viza}} per year: from you or your family.

sections.title: What your school certificate or diploma qualifies you for
items: 11-year school certificate: a bachelor's degree in Italy usually requires 12 years of schooling. There are two ways: a Foundation year (at Sapienza, Pavia, Padova, Messina and others) or studying for 1 year at a university in Uzbekistan and then applying.
12 years of schooling (lyceum, college) or 1st year of university: you apply directly for a bachelor's degree.
Bachelor's degree: you apply for a master's. The subjects you studied in your bachelor's must match the chosen master's.
Medicine: admission follows a separate procedure, places are limited and the rules have changed in recent years. Check the university's bando every year.

sections.title: Language and tests
items: English: many programmes ask for B2 (IELTS about 5.5–6.5, depending on the programme). Get the certificate before applications open.
CEnT-S: a test required by many bachelor's programmes. It can be taken from home; the last announced price is 55 €.
TOLC: for Italian-taught programmes, 35 € (2026). The English versions of TOLC have been replaced by CEnT-S.
SAT, GMAT or GRE: required by some programmes (for example private universities).
To know exactly which test you need, read the admission page of your chosen university. Every university page on our site has an «Admission and requirements» section.

chapters.tip: Apply to 3–5 universities, not just one. Their deadlines differ: if one is late or rejects you, there is another.

links.label: Find a university that suits me

chapters.title: University application and pre-acceptance
chapters.when: Usually November – April, different at each university
chapters.body:
Pre-acceptance is the university's answer «we are ready to admit you». Without it none of the next steps can start: neither Universitaly nor the visa.

Each university has its own online portal and its own deadline. You register on the portal, complete your profile, upload documents and pay the application fee (if there is one). Then the committee reviews it. The answer can take anywhere from a few weeks to a few months.
steps: Find your chosen programme on the university page and read its requirements: deadline, fee, required test.
Register on the application portal. Use the same email everywhere: later the letters from the university, Universitaly and the embassy will come to that address.
Complete your profile and upload documents as clear colour PDFs.
Pay the application fee: unpaid applications are not reviewed. Usually 0–70 € at state universities and 100–150 € at private ones.
Wait for the answer and keep an eye on your email. As soon as pre-acceptance arrives, move on to chapters 3 and 4.

sections.title: Documents usually requested
items: International passport
School certificate or diploma
Certificate from your school or university (if you are studying now: where, and in which grade or year)
Transcript (record of grades)
Language certificate (usually B2)
If the programme asks: CV, motivation letter, test result (SAT, CEnT-S, TOLC, GMAT)
Optional: recommendation letter

sections.title: How to write a motivation letter
items: Do not copy a template. The committee reads hundreds of identical letters, and yours should be your own story.
Answer three questions: why exactly this field, why exactly this university, what you want to do after your studies.
Give a concrete example: a project, an olympiad, work experience, an event that brought you to this field.
Keep it short: one page is usually enough. If the university sets a word count, stick to it.
Have someone read it before you send it.

chapters.tip: Do not wait for the last day. Portals slow down in the final days, and in some programmes places run out early.
chapters.warn: If scans are blurry or incomplete, the application may be rejected. Scan every page in full, clearly and in colour.

chapters.title: Diploma recognition: DoV or CIMEA
chapters.body:
Italy needs to know what your school certificate or diploma is equivalent to in its system. There are two ways, and your university will tell you which one it needs.

The DoV (Dichiarazione di Valore) is issued by the consular section of the Italian Embassy in Tashkent. CIMEA is an online organisation: you apply yourself on the DiploMe platform and the certificate arrives electronically.

In both cases you first get your documents apostilled in Uzbekistan and translated into Italian. Uzbekistan is a party to the Hague Convention, so an apostille is enough.
steps: Get an apostille on your school certificate or diploma, transcript and certificate from your school or university.
Have the translation into Italian done by a trusted translator from the embassy's list. A translation by a translator not on the list may not be accepted.
For DoV: fill in the form from the embassy website and hand in the documents at the consular section. Another person can submit with a power of attorney.
For CIMEA: register yourself on cimea-diplome.it (applications through intermediaries are not accepted), choose your diploma in the Service Finder, upload the documents and pay.
Upload the finished DoV or CIMEA certificate to your university and to Universitaly.

sections.title: Documents (DoV and CIMEA)
items: Passport copy
School certificate or diploma
Transcript (record of grades)
Certificate from your school or university
Language certificate
Apostilled and translated into Italian: school certificate or diploma, transcript and certificate from your school or university
Additionally for DoV: completed application form and Universitaly pre-enrollment form

sections.title: Processing time and price
items: CIMEA: Comparability and Verification together 300 € (for many countries), in some cases 150 €. The system shows the price itself.
Standard CIMEA processing time: 60 working days, about 3 months.
Fast track: +100 €, Comparability in 30 working days. It can only be chosen when applying.
The cost of apostille and translation depends on the number of documents and the translator.

chapters.tip: Never leave this stage until the end. CIMEA takes 3 months, and without it your visa documents are incomplete. Start the very day pre-acceptance arrives.
chapters.warn: Some universities (for example Messina's Early Bird round) ask for DoV or CIMEA already at the application stage. Read your university's conditions in advance.

chapters.when: By the deadline set by the university (usually spring – summer)
chapters.body:
Universitaly is the single portal of the Italian Ministry of Education. Here you submit the pre-enrollment application for your chosen programme. The university checks and confirms it (validation), after which it goes to the embassy. Without a confirmed pre-enrollment you cannot apply for the visa.

Each university sets its own deadline. For example, in the 2026/27 academic year these deadlines ranged from 30 June to 15 September, depending on the university.

At some universities pre-acceptance and pre-enrollment happen in one step: once the university reviews and accepts your application, it also confirms the pre-enrollment on Universitaly or includes it in the admission process. Then you do not need to do anything separately. Check how your university works on its admission page or by email. Either way, to apply for the visa you must have a confirmed pre-enrollment in your name on Universitaly: check it in your Universitaly account.
steps: Register on universitaly.it (with the same email as on the university portal).
Fill in the pre-enrollment form: personal details, university and programme, scans of passport and diploma.
Choose the programme name exactly as in the pre-acceptance letter.
Wait for the university to confirm. Download and print the PDF summary of the confirmed application: it is on the list of visa documents.
The embassy sends you a letter about applying for the visa. Then move on to chapter 6.
chapters.tip: Apply early. Universities can confirm on Universitaly at most 20% more applications than their quota. When places run out, latecomers are left out.
chapters.warn: Do not book a visa appointment before the university confirms: an unconfirmed application is not valid for the visa.

chapters.title: Scholarship (DSU): the biggest opportunity
chapters.when: Application usually June – September, depending on the region
chapters.body:
Something many people do not know: in Italy regional agencies give scholarships to students from low-income families. This applies to foreign students too. The scholarship includes money, in many cities meals and accommodation (in some regions these are paid out of the scholarship), and a tuition fee waiver.

The state minimum for the 2026/27 academic year for a student living away from their family (fuori sede) is {{stip}} per year. Regions may give more.

The most important point: you apply in summer, while you are still in Uzbekistan. And the family documents can only be prepared in Uzbekistan. So you start this before you leave.
steps: Find out which region your university is in and its scholarship agency (DiSCo in Lazio, DSU Toscana in Tuscany, and so on).
Read the agency's bando (the document with the conditions): deadline, amount, required documents.
Get your family documents in Uzbekistan, have them legalised at the Italian Embassy (or apostilled; ask the agency or a CAF in advance which one is accepted) and translated into Italian.
Apply online on the agency's portal (usually in summer).
After arriving in Italy, you have your ISEE parificato calculated at a CAF centre and upload the documents the agency asks for (permesso, IBAN) to the portal.

sections.title: Family documents to obtain in Uzbekistan (Lazio example)
items: Family composition and residence: name, date of birth and permanent address of each member.
Annual income of each family member. For a member who does not work, a document stating this clearly.
Housing: whether family members own property and its size (cadastre certificate).
Bank: savings of each member (if none, a document stating so).
Rental contract: only if the family rents.
Everything must be legalised at the Italian Embassy (or apostilled) and translated into Italian.

sections.title: Limits (2026/27)
items: ISEE limit: {{isee}}, ISPE limit: {{ispe}}. If either is exceeded, no scholarship is given.
Scholarship winners are exempt from tuition fees.
From the second year you need to have earned enough credits (CFU) to receive the scholarship.

chapters.tip: Take the scholarship into account when choosing a university: the amount, meals and accommodation conditions differ by region.
chapters.warn: An application written by yourself, an affidavit or a sworn statement is not accepted. The family's total income cannot be zero. Applying for a scholarship does not count as proof of funds for the visa.

chapters.title: Student visa (type D)
chapters.when: From 6 months to 15 days before travel. For 2027/28 at the latest 31.10.2027
chapters.body:
The student visa is submitted to the consular section of the Italian Embassy in Tashkent. It is a type D national visa: 91 to 365 days, multiple entry. Processing takes up to 90 days, and your passport stays at the embassy all that time.

The part of the visa that raises the most questions is money. You must show that you have {{viza}} per year (the 2026/27 and 2027/28 requirement). This money is not spent: you show that it is in your account or your family's.
steps: Wait for your Universitaly pre-enrollment to be confirmed.
Collect the documents according to the embassy list (below).
Get the bank statement last: on the day you apply it must not be older than 10 working days.
Submit to the consular section: not earlier than 6 months and not later than 15 days before travel.
Wait for the answer. Your passport is not returned until a decision is made, so do not plan other trips for that time.

sections.title: Documents
items: Signed visa application form and 1 photo (white background, not older than 6 months)
Passport: issued within the last 10 years, valid for 90 more days after the visa expires, at least 2 blank pages. Copy of passport and ID
Certificate of residence (my.gov.uz)
Copy of the Universitaly pre-enrollment and the university's admission letter
Receipt of at least the first payment
Language certificate, diploma and transcript (original, copy and Italian translation), DoV or CIMEA

Money: bank statement for the last 3 months (on bank letterhead, with a wet stamp), international card statement, certificate of employment and salary, and if there is a sponsor, their letter of no objection
Insurance: at least 30 000 €, for the whole Schengen area and the whole period
Accommodation for the first month: booking or an invitation from a person in Italy
Return ticket booking

sections.title: An honest word about money
items: The money must come from a legal, traceable source: your own account or your family's (relatives up to the 4th degree).
The embassy checks the account activity and whether the amount matches the family's income. A large sum that suddenly appears in the last days raises questions.
So prepare the money in advance, in a way that can be explained.

chapters.tip: Before anything else, check your passport's validity. It must be valid for 90 more days after the visa expires. Replacing a passport takes time.
chapters.warn: You cannot enrol at a university on a tourist visa, only on a type D student visa. A university may also set a deadline earlier than the embassy's.

chapters.title: Getting ready for the trip
chapters.when: After the visa, before you fly
chapters.body: The visa is in your hands. Congratulations, one of the hardest parts is behind you! Now prepare calmly: the first weeks in Italy are spent on bureaucracy, and if you have the right papers with you, everything goes much more smoothly.
steps: Take all original documents and their translations with you: diploma, transcript, DoV or CIMEA, passport, insurance.
Keep 2–3 copies of each and scans on your phone.

Find housing before you arrive in Italy: this is students' biggest problem, good rooms are booked early. Ask the university's housing office and Uzbek students in that city. At least for the first weeks, have a place (dormitory, hostel) booked.
Have your own money for the first 3–4 months: the scholarship is usually paid late and in instalments.
Put the deadlines of the university and the scholarship agency in your calendar.
chapters.tip: Get to know Uzbek students at that university in advance. They will help a lot with the city, housing and the first days.
chapters.warn: Do not transfer money without seeing the place and signing a contract. An ad saying «I am abroad, I will send the keys by post» is a classic scam.

links.label: Living in Italy: housing, health, work

chapters.title: You have arrived in Italy: the first week
chapters.when: From the day you arrive, permesso within 8 working days
chapters.body:
The visa lets you enter Italy, but the right to live there comes from the permesso di soggiorno (residence permit). You must request it within 8 working days of arrival. This is a legal requirement, do not delay.

Below everything is in the order it is done. Housing should have been found earlier, before you came to Italy (chapter 7).
steps: Get a SIM card: at a TIM, Vodafone, WindTre or Iliad shop, with your passport. An Italian number is needed for the permesso, the bank and the university.
Get a public transport card: a monthly or yearly pass from the city transport company. Many cities have student discounts.
Buy a 16 € marca da bollo (revenue stamp) at a Tabaccheria (tobacco shop).

At a Poste Italiane (post office) branch marked «Sportello Amico», get the yellow kit (package) for your first permesso. Fill in and sign Form 1, and add copies of your passport and visa, insurance and financial documents, and the marca da bollo.
Hand in the kit at the post office and get the receipt (ricevuta): until the card arrives, it is your document.
Get your codice fiscale (tax code): at an Agenzia delle Entrate office, with passport and visa, free of charge. If it was issued earlier, you do not need a new one.
Open a bank account (IBAN): the scholarship is paid into it. You need a codice fiscale for this.
The Questura will call you for fingerprints. The card is usually ready about 90 days after that.
Once you have the permesso receipt: full enrollment (next chapter). A codice fiscale is not required for it.

sections.title: Optional but very useful: the tessera sanitaria
items: This is the Italian health card: you choose a family doctor (medico di base) and use public clinics and hospitals like Italians do.
To get it you register with the Italian national health service (SSN): {{ssn}} per year for students (per calendar year).
Go to the local ASL office with your permesso receipt and codice fiscale.
If you do not register with the SSN, you must have private insurance valid in Italy for the whole period.

chapters.tip: Always carry copies of all your documents. Queues at the Questura, post office and bank can be long: be patient, it is the same for everyone.
chapters.warn: Do not lose the post office receipt. It is asked for both at full enrollment and at the scholarship agency.

links.label: Living in Italy: housing, health, work

chapters.title: Full enrollment: becoming a full student
chapters.when: After arrival, by the deadline set by the university
chapters.body: The last official step. You take your original documents to the university's international students office, complete the payments and receive your student number. Many universities ask for this within about a month of arrival.
steps: Find your university's international students office and its opening hours.
Bring the documents: passport, «University enrolment» student visa, permesso receipt, diploma (with official translation), DoV or CIMEA.

Make the first payment on time: usually the regional scholarship tax (tassa regionale, 140 € in many regions) and a 16 € bollo, and at some universities a university contribution too. The amount depends on the university, for example at least 156 € at Sapienza. If you miss the deadline in the 1st year, you cannot register at all at Sapienza; if other payments are late, a fine is added (65 € at Sapienza). If you are a scholarship winner, you are exempt from tuition fees.
Get your student number and university account.
Upload your enrollment and permesso documents to the scholarship agency's portal (by the agency's deadline).
chapters.tip: Keep separate track of the scholarship agency's deadlines: for example, in 2026/27 Lazio DiSCo asked for the permesso and ISEE documents by 10.12.2026.

chapters.title: Life in Italy: what to know in advance
chapters.body: Italy is a beautiful country, but the first year is not easy. If you know this in advance, when difficulties come you will not think «I did something wrong»: it happens to everyone.

sections.title: Work
items: With a student permesso you can work officially up to 20 hours a week (1 040 hours a year).
The employer must sign an official contract. Undeclared work can cause problems when renewing the permesso.
Universities have paid part-time jobs for students.

sections.title: Studies and documents
items: Put your classes first: to keep the scholarship next year, you need credits (CFU).
You renew the permesso before it expires.
You reapply for the scholarship every year.
With an Italian permesso you can travel to other Schengen countries for up to 90 days within 180 days.

sections.title: Everyday life
items: Even if your programme is in English, you will need Italian in everyday life: aim for A2–B1.
Housing in big cities is expensive and scarce. Start looking early.
Loneliness and homesickness are natural. Student associations, university events and the Uzbek student community help.

chapters.tip: After graduating, if the conditions are met, the student permesso can be converted into a job-seeking permesso for up to 12 months.

mistakes: Applying to only one university. Apply to 3–5.
Waiting for the last day. Portals slow down, and CIMEA takes 3 months.
Using different emails. Letters from the university, Universitaly and the embassy should go to one address.
Getting the bank statement too early. On the day you apply it must not be older than 10 working days.
Looking for scholarship documents after arriving in Italy. Prepare them in Uzbekistan, with legalisation (or apostille) and translation.
Delaying the permesso. Apply within 8 days of arrival.
Believing «a friend told me» posts on social media. Always check the official source.
closing:
If you have read this far, you are already ahead of most people. Now you see the whole path and know when each step comes.

Remember: requirements and dates change every year and depend on the university and region. This guide is a general roadmap, not a guarantee. Check the official source before each step.

If you have questions or need help submitting documents, write to us on Telegram. Good luck!
